Summary: EU-based contact center platform (multichannel: voice, chat, email) evaluating Redwood for agent-assist + RAG over support KBs. Goal: replace brittle keyword search with cited, fresh RAG answers for agents and automated ticket triage.

Recent activity:
- 2026-01-15 discovery call w/ Maya (AE) + Diego (SE). high-level ask: reduce average handle time (AHT) by 20% and deflect 15% of tickets.

Requirements / success criteria (customer-stated):
- Use-cases: live agent assist (streamed suggestions), post-call ticket summarization, automated tool-calling (CRM updates via function calls).
- RAG: multi-source retrieval (Zendesk, Confluence, KB PDFs, internal DB), citation tied to answer, freshness window <= 48 hours for product incidents.
- Accuracy/quality targets: citation precision >= 0.85, helpfulness NPS uplift +7 pts in pilot.
- Latency/throughput: median first-token latency <= 250ms for agent-assist; tail p95 < 400ms; support burst to 2,000 reqs/min with sub-second responses.
- Cost sensitivity: moderate — willing to pay for Dedicated capacity for reliability during spikes; Optimize recommendations required to justify ARR.
- Models: prefer open/quantized stacks for private runs (13B/70B quantized variants), but open to hosted short-term for quick wins.
- Deployment: must run in EU VPC or on-premises for regulated customers; SSO (SAML) + SCIM user provisioning; full audit logs + retention controls.

POC notes / technical observations:
- POC used hybrid retrieval: keyword recall + dense embeddings improved citation coverage on long-tail KB pages.
- Current vector index (single node) shows warming latency under spike — SE recommended Redwood Dedicated with autoscaling and prefix KV caching.
- Tool-calling: demoed safe CRM patch flow (sandbox) — need final approval from automation/compliance team for write-backs.
- Freshness: ingestion pipeline must support incremental updates from Zendesk + Confluence; customer expects near-real-time ingestion for incident pages.
